Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:75: And to understand the matter further, we say that the foods mentioned there in the teachings are four: the first, the food of the people in general, from heaven and earth, meaning that their sustenance is prepared for them and they eat their sufficiency whenever they need. The second, the food of the poor, from the attribute of Justice [Tzedek]. The third, the food of the sick, from the attribute called "heaven," as it is said (Psalms 41:4), "the LORD will sustain him on the bed of illness." The fourth, the food of the Torah scholar, from the side of Chokhmah - each one according to the preparation of the refinement of his body and soul, so shall the supernal spirituality be bestowed and rest upon him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:76: Now, the poor - their food is from the attribute of Tzedek, because they are "of broken spirit," and their heart is broken and crushed - so their food is finer, because their food is not found and prepared for them whenever they wish; therefore a flow is bestowed upon them from the attribute of Tzedek, that their food be blessed and they have sustenance until the time their food arrives.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:77: And the sick, who do not eat bread at all, but only some drink, and sometimes do not even drink a drink, and their food is the shrinking of the fat and blood within them - their food is more spiritual, since the powers of the body have already ceased, and from the side of the supernal attribute mentioned, sustenance is bestowed to their soul.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:78: And Torah scholars occupied with Torah - their food is entirely food for the soul, meaning that the Shechinah bestows their food from Chokhmah, as it says (Proverbs 31:14), "she brings her bread from afar." And it is already known that the word "far" and "distances" is always [a term for] the Name - and this bread is physical, being the bread of their food through which their body is sustained, but there is in that bread a supernal spirituality, such that one meal of it suffices to give the body sustenance for three days and the like, and it has spirituality for the comprehension of Torah and its secrets. And a proof of this is what they said in the Zohar (Parashat Lech Lecha, page 94b) concerning the village of Tarsha, where they said to Rabbi Abba that that place merited them concerning the matter of Torah, and he said, "this is our way: half the night we sleep and half we occupy ourselves with Torah, and when we stand in the morning, the scents of the field and the flowing rivers illuminate Torah for us and it settles in our heart" - to this point, relevant here. Behold, it is explicit that the scents of the field would illuminate for them the secrets of the Torah. And the reason is that through the occupation with Torah in which they engaged in that place, the Holy One, blessed be He, would bring down spiritual flow into those grasses, and through this they attained wisdom - and this is likewise the way concerning the food of Torah scholars: a flow of soul-food for the comprehension of Torah is bestowed in that bread or in other foods.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:79: And this is what is explained in the Tikkunim (page 45b), which we copied in the Gate of Love (chapter 6): the Shechinah has one to whom she brings down the food of the body, and has one to whom she brings down the food of the soul, which is the food of Torah. And one should not explain that it is the food of Torah alone, for if he did not eat at all he would die - rather, the intent is that most of his food is food for the soul, and even though he eats bodily food, since it is fine, the soul is the one nourished and grows strong in the comprehension of Torah, while the body is weak.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:80: And support for this matter we find in the Zohar (Parashat Vayera, page 104a) - these are its words: they said there that the angels who visited Abraham our father, peace be upon him, everything they ate was consumed by fire, and although it is written in the verse that they ate, the intent is the food they were nourished by from the kindness of Abraham. And it says, and therefore it is written "and they ate" - it caused them to be nourished from the side of Abraham, and therefore nothing remained of what Abraham gave them. In the same way, a person needs to drink from that cup of blessing, in order to merit that supernal blessing - they too ate from what Abraham prepared for them in order to merit being nourished from the side of Abraham, for from that side sustenance goes forth to all the supernal angels - to this point. Behold, it is explicit that although nothing remained of the physical food they ate, since it was consumed by fire, nevertheless they were spiritually nourished from the side of the kindness they ate through Abraham. And so it is with the food of Torah scholars: even though the food in their body is digested, spiritual food remains for their soul, because their food is bestowed from Chokhmah, which is above Chesed, and they can stand without eating three or four days, and while they are occupied with Torah they are nourished by the spirituality of that Torah in which they are engaged. If so, without doubt this matter is found only among those whose Torah is their sole occupation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:81: And in this way it is settled how Rashbi, peace be upon him, and his son sat in a cave thirteen years and were nourished by eating carobs (Shabbat 33b), because the supernal attribute of Chokhmah was their food, and it is finer and more spiritual than all the other, lower attributes, and does not rest in the body because of its fineness, but rather gives spiritual food to ru'ach and neshamah, which are [the level of] Torah scholars - for the ordinary Torah scholar who holds the middle line has ru'ach and neshamah, and therefore his food from above is fine and spiritual. And so we find they said in the Tikkunim that Chokhmah is the "sap of the tree," and it is the "soul of life" (Tikkunei Zohar, page 96a), spreading within the attributes to give them life, and it does not rest within the attributes except as the spreading of Da'at and Binah within them, as my teacher, peace be upon him, explained in the Idra. And therefore Torah scholars who hold fast to Torah hold fast to the root and foundation, for Torah is more internal than all the commandments, as shall be explained in its place, and their food is Chokhmah, and it rests only in their ru'ach and neshamah, not in the body, even though they eat - and therefore the soul grows strong and the body is weak.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:82: And because the essential food of Torah scholars is for the soul, as explained, therefore they can stand two or three days without eating at all, since the food of Torah is their food, and it is what gives them sustenance. And if this matter is found among penitents, we can say that the power of repentance is what nourishes them, as it is written in the Tikkunim (page 113b) that penitents have an additional soul, and this additional soul, which is through the power of repentance, can nourish them so that they stand three days without eating - and likewise the attribute of the righteous, to content themselves with little, for the reason mentioned.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:83: And the general teaching concerning the matter of intent is that a person should think, at the time of eating, that he is eating before the King, and that his eating is bestowed from the table that is before the LORD, and through this he shall not come to be a glutton - for they compared, in the Zohar, the lower table to the supernal table: so it is found that just as from the supernal table the supernal souls and angels are nourished, so his soul is nourished from the supernal food materialized in this lower table - and this is (Proverbs 13:25), "the righteous eats to satisfy his soul."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:84: And there is necessity for this intent from the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, page 156b), on the verse (Psalms 23:5), "You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies" - these are its words: a person's table merits him to eat at another table in the delight of that [World to Come], as it is said (II Samuel 9:13), "for he always ate at the king's table" - and King David said, "You prepare a table before me," meaning the arrangement of the table exists in that world, for then it is the delight and longing that the soul enjoys for the World to Come. And do souls have a table in that world? Yes - for they eat food and the sufficiency of delight in that world, just as the supernal angels eat, and do they eat of supernal bread? Yes, see there - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:85: And along these lines, in his eating he should intend that his eating comes from the Shechinah, from whom the food is bestowed downward to those below, that all eating in this world - and although eating is found above too - "eat, friends" (Song of Songs 5:1) - they already answered this in Parashat Vayikra (Zohar, page 4a): whoever has jugs of wine still needs to eat.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:86: Further, one can explain the matter of the intent of eating by what they, of blessed memory, said - that the table is called an altar. They said in Berachot (54b): Rabbi Yehudah said, three things prolong a person's days and years: one who prolongs his prayer, one who lingers at his table, and one who lingers in the privy - and there they explained the proof for each one, and gave the reason for lingering at one's table: perhaps a poor person will come and he will give to him, for it is written (Ezekiel 41:22), "the altar of wood, three cubits high," and it is written (ibid.), "and he said to me, this is the table that is before the LORD" - it opens with "altar" and concludes with "table." Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar both said, as long as the Temple stood, the altar atoned for Israel, and now a person's table atones for him - to this point. And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said: Rabbi Elazar said, when the Temple stood, the altar atoned for him, and now that the Temple does not stand, his table, when merited, atones for him, as it is said (Isaiah 58:7), "is it not to share your bread with the hungry" - if not merited, "and bring the wretched poor into your house" - meaning, non-Jews come and take by force - to this point. Now, according to the plain sense of this teaching, if at the start of his eating he directs his intent that from that eating he shall give to a poor person, his eating is a mitzvah and the soul enjoys such a meal - and along these lines we can explain in a second way, (Proverbs 13:25) "the righteous eats to satisfy his soul": that when he eats with the intent to perform a mitzvah from that meal, so that his soul be satisfied from the mitzvah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:87: And they already elaborated at length in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, page 155b) on the merit of feeding the poor at one's table. They, of blessed memory, said: through what does a person merit to delight in that supernal delight? Through his table, through what he delights upon his table the souls of the poor, as it is written (Isaiah 58:10), "and satisfy the afflicted soul" - what is written after it? "then you shall delight in the LORD" - for likewise the Holy One, blessed be He, shall satiate him with all those delights of the anointing oil of the supernal holiness that flows and is drawn continually to that supernal glory - to this point. And this is "to satisfy his soul" - that just as he satiated the afflicted soul, so too his own soul shall be satisfied from the supernal light.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:88: However, this is fine when it is possible to merit [giving] to a poor person; but if a person is traveling on the road and there is no poor person with him, or in a place where poor people are not commonly found - such as at night, when there are not so many poor people going about, or in a place where poor people are not found - what is his remedy so that the table become an altar? One could say that he should estimate in his mind the value of the food that the poor person could have eaten, and give him the money with which the poor person could buy the necessities of a meal - and this is a fine device - and he should choose to give his bread or his money to a poor person who has some knowledge of Torah, and who knows to bless the Grace After Meals and the other blessings of enjoyment, and then the charity is desirable, as we shall elaborate in its place.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:89: However, this device is from the way of the intellect, and the Gemara said only "perhaps a poor person will come and he will give to him" - the essential point being that he give from his own portion to the poor person, as it is written, "is it not to share your bread with the hungry" - from what you yourself eat. And moreover, it is difficult: the poor person himself, who does not have enough for his own sufficiency alone, how shall his own table atone for him?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:90: And one could answer with what is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, page 153b) - these are its words: every person's table must always be before him when he blesses the Holy One, blessed be He, so that blessing rest upon it from above, and it not be seen empty - for supernal blessings do not rest in an empty place, as it is written (II Kings 4:2), "tell me, what do you have in the house" - and the colleagues have already established that a table upon which words of Torah were not said, of it is written (Isaiah 28:8), "for all tables are full of vomit and filth, without a place" - and it is forbidden to bless over that table. Why? Because there is a table and a table: there is a table which one arranges before the Holy One, blessed be He, above, and it stands always ready to arrange upon it the words of Torah and to include within it the letters of the words of Torah, and it gathers them within itself and includes all of them within itself, and through them it is perfected and rejoices and has joy - and of this table it is written (Ezekiel 41:22), "this is the table that is before the LORD" - "before the LORD" and not "of before the LORD." There is another table that has no portion in Torah and has no portion in the holiness of Torah, and this is "without a place," for it has no portion at all in the side of holiness - therefore a table upon which words of Torah were not said is a table of "vomit and filth," it is a table of another god, that table has no portion in the secret of the supernal God. A table upon which words of Torah were said - the Holy One, blessed be He, takes that table and makes it His own portion, and moreover, the great appointed angel Suriya takes those words and forms an image of that table before the Holy One, blessed be He, and all those words of Torah said over it ascend upon that table, and it is set ready before the Holy One, blessed be He, the Holy King - implying what is written, "this is the table that is before the LORD," that it is set ready before the Holy One, blessed be He. A person's table stands to purify him from all his sins.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:91: Happy is he who has these two things standing upon his table: words of Torah, and a portion for the poor from that table. When that table is cleared away from before a person, two holy angels present themselves there, one from his right and one from his left - one says, this is the table of the Holy King that so-and-so arranges before Him; may this table always be arranged with supernal blessings and supernal anointing oil and greatness, may the Holy One, blessed be He, rest upon it - and one says, this is the table of the Holy King that so-and-so arranges before Him; this is a table that supernal and lower beings shall bless him for; may this table be arranged before the Ancient of Days in this world and in the World to Come. When Abba would clear away the table from before him, he would cover it, and would say, clear away this table modestly, so that it not be shamed before the King's messengers. A person's table merits him the World to Come, and merits him the sustenance of this world, and merits him to be recognized favorably before the Ancient of Days, and merits him to add strength and greatness in the place it is needed - happy is the portion of that person in this world and in the World to Come - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:92: Behold, it said that a person's table stands to purify him from all his sins - and this certainly refers to the occupation with Torah at the table before the Grace After Meals, for they said, a table upon which words of Torah were not said, it is forbidden to bless over that table - it seems this certainly refers to before the Grace After Meals. And this also demolishes the view of one who wrote that through the Grace After Meals one fulfills the obligation of saying words of Torah at a table that lacked them, as explained. And up to now it did not speak of the portion for the poor, but afterward it said, happy is he who has these two things standing upon his table - and we have already explained above that the nature of the word "happy" [zakai] means "more praiseworthy." It follows that in every place where there are no poor, or he himself is poor, his table shall be an altar to atone for his sins through his occupation with Torah, and it is fitting that it be called an altar - for just as the altar is called an altar because sacrifices are slaughtered upon it, so through the occupation with Torah a person slaughters his inclination, as they said (Sukkah 52b), if this despicable one accosts you, drag him to the study hall; if he is [hard as] a stone, he shall melt. And Torah also atones for sins more than all sacrifices, as it is said (I Samuel 3:14), "if the iniquity of the house of Eli be atoned by sacrifice or meal-offering" - and they explained (Rosh Hashanah 18a): but it is atoned by words of Torah - for words of Torah are superior to all sacrifices, as explained in Parashat Kedoshim (page 80b), see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:93: And in Midrash Ruth (5:15), they, of blessed memory, said (Ruth 3:7), "and Boaz ate and drank, and his heart was merry" - why "and his heart was merry"? Because he blessed over his food. Another explanation: "and his heart was merry" - that he ate sweet things after the meal, which accustoms the tongue to Torah. Another explanation: "and his heart was merry" - that he occupied himself with words of Torah, as it is said (Psalms 119:72), "the Torah of Your mouth is better to me" - to this point; and one could say all of these are true.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:94: Also, if he is a penitent, let him confess before he eats - this too is slaughtering his inclination. And so Rabbeinu Yonah wrote in Sefer HaYirah, that a penitent needs to confess beforehand and examine what he has done up until that hour. And through this he shall not come to be a glutton, for he shall think of his many sins, and that he is not worthy, because of his sins, of that food, but rather it is due to the great kindness of Him who sustains the wicked and the good alike. And this is the matter (Pesachim 118a) that a person's sustenance is as difficult as the splitting of the Sea of Reeds - as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, page 170a), that it is difficult before the Holy One, blessed be He, meaning the Shechinah who judges the world to sustain it, because of the wickedness of its deeds. Behold, through this he slaughters his inclination, and the table becomes for him an atoning altar.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:95: Also, Rabbeinu Yonah wrote (there) that while he still craves to eat, he should refrain from his desires for the honor of the Creator. This too is slaughtering his inclination and is atoned for him, for he certainly slaughters his physical desire, and it is written (Psalms 50:23), "whoever sacrifices thanksgiving honors Me" - and they, of blessed memory, explained (Sanhedrin 43b) that whoever slaughters his inclination and confesses honors the Holy One, blessed be He, in both worlds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:96: And from the whole of the Zohar teaching we have copied, you shall see the greatness of the early sages, peace be upon them, for they considered matters according to their spirituality, not according to their physicality - for they said that they would cover the table so that it be done modestly, and this is because of the spirituality of the holiness upon it, since it became a foundation for holiness in that words of Torah were said over it and a portion was given from it to the poor - and the spirituality of the mitzvah performed at that table is that the angels raise it up, and the two angels, one corresponding to the Torah and the second, the portion for the poor - the one corresponding to the portion for the poor blesses him with the blessings of the world, measure for measure, and this is what it said, "may this table always be arranged with supernal blessings." And corresponding to the Torah it said, this is the table of the Holy King - being the holy Torah bestowed from it, ascending up higher and higher - and therefore it said, "may this table be arranged before the Ancient of Days."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:97: And what it said at the end of the teaching, "and merits him to add strength and greatness in the place it is needed" - this refers to the Shechinah, who needs the arousal of those below, and before whom sustenance is difficult, as explained; and therefore, since these two things - Torah and charity - are dedicated to her, they add strength to her from above, for these two have their essence in the Tree of Life, and all are from the side of the right.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:98: "The Torah" - explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, end of page 245), which said that the table is a judgment in the north, and one must bind to it the Torah, which is from the right - these are its words: but in the secrets of Torah they established, whoever wishes to become wealthy should face north; he should place his table in the north. Behold, the table is to the left, being judgment, and it needs to be bound with the right, which is Torah, given from Chesed, which is mercy - "the right hand of the LORD" - to this point. And in the Zohar (Parashat Eikev, page 273) they explained concerning this matter, that Torah is YHVH from the right, the table is Adonai from the left - it follows that the intent is the unification of the two Names, YAHDONHY [YHVH-Adonai combined], "then you shall call and the LORD shall answer" (Isaiah 58:9).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:99: And likewise charity is the Tree of Life, explained in Parashat Bechukotai (page 113b), and in several other places, and we shall copy its words in its place. And there (Zohar, Parashat Beshalach, page 62a), that charity, which is the bestowal of loving-kindness from the side of Chesed - they, of blessed memory, said, the food that is more supernal than it, that which is finer, comes from the place where judgment resides, and is called Tzedek, and this is the food of the poor - and the secret of the matter: whoever completes [gives] to a poor person completes for him the letter Yud, and it becomes Tzedakah [charity], and this is the secret, "a man of kindness does good to his own soul" [gomel nafsho ish chesed] - implying "acts of kindness" [gemilut chasadim] - for it resides in judgment and completes it with kindness, and then it is mercy - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:100: It follows that through these two commandments, one gives strength above, and through this we shall explain a third explanation of "the righteous eats to satisfy his soul" - to give satisfaction to his supernal soul through Torah and charity, along the lines of what is explained in the Zohar (there, Parashat Terumah, page 128b), "the rock of my heart and my portion" (Psalms 73:26), and "a merry heart" (Proverbs 15:15), and "his heart was merry" (Ruth 3:7) - all of these are said of the Holy One, blessed be He; likewise we say that "his soul" is said of the Holy One, blessed be He, and this is to add strength and greatness to the place it is needed, as we have explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:101: Further, I have heard another way, that all his meals should be for the sake of a mitzvah, and that he should do as Shammai the Elder used to do, of whom they said that all his days he would eat in honor of the Sabbath - how so? If he found a fine animal, he would say, this is for the honor of the Sabbath; if he found another finer than it, and so on (Beitzah 16a) - it follows from this device that his meal is a mitzvah, for sometimes he shall need to restrain his desires for the honor of the Sabbath, such as if he did not find another finer than it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:102: And one must understand what praise this is - for at first glance it would have been better to leave both the first and the second for the Sabbath, and what benefit is there in eating the first one that was designated for the honor of the Sabbath? And also, if it did not happen that he found another finer than it, it follows that he would not eat in honor of the Sabbath at all, and it would have been fitting to say that all his days he would set aside [an animal] for the Sabbath.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:103: But in truth this is not a difficulty, for certainly, if the second animal would not have sufficed for the Sabbath, he certainly would have left both of them - rather, certainly the second one would have sufficed for him, and therefore he ate the first one.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:104: And the reason for the possibility of this matter is found in what they said in the Mechilta (Parashat Yitro), concerning "remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy" (Exodus 20:8) - you shall remember it from the first day of the week, so that if a fine portion happens to come to you, you shall designate it for the sake of the Sabbath - and we copied the rest of its words above, in chapter 2, and this was the reasoning of Shammai the Elder. And so they said there in the Gemara: it was likewise taught, Beit Shammai say, from the first day of your week, to your Sabbath; and Beit Hillel say (Psalms 68:20), "blessed is the LORD, day by day He bears our burden" - and Rashi, peace be upon him, explained: "from the first day of your week, to your Sabbath" - from the first day of your week, set your heart toward the coming Sabbath. And we have already explained there (chapter 2) the reason for the possibility of remembering the Sabbath every day, and that reason shall suffice for the possibility of this designation - but concerning the matter of eating, we can say, as explained there, that a person's eating on the Sabbath is not equal to his eating on a weekday, for the eating of the Sabbath is called "Oneg" [delight], and it is the secret of "Eden, river, garden," as it is said (Isaiah 58:13), "and call the Sabbath a delight [oneg]," and it is a mitzvah. Now, by designating on the first day of the week a portion for the Sabbath, holiness of the Sabbath already rests upon it, and when he finds another finer than it for the Sabbath and eats the first one, it follows that he refines his eating with the holiness of Sabbath eating, which is spiritual eating and a mitzvah - and one of the things that save the body of the righteous from being ruled over by worms at their death is that they derive enjoyment only from a meal of mitzvah and the meals of Sabbaths and festivals, and at the very least this one shall enjoy that it not be said, "take what you chose," for he derived enjoyment only from a meal of mitzvah, which is the Sabbath.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:105: And if you say, but if a fine portion did not happen to come to him, it follows that he would not eat in honor of the Sabbath at all - one can say that the Holy One, blessed be He, joins a good thought to the deed (Kiddushin 40a), and this is why it brought, "it was likewise taught, from the first day of your week, to your Sabbath," and Rashi, of blessed memory, explained, "set your heart toward the coming Sabbath" - and it did not say that he should by all means seek to designate for the Sabbath, but rather that he should set his heart that the first portion that happens to come to him shall be for the Sabbath.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:106: And this matter is exactly what is explained in the Mechilta on "remember" - that the remembering is in the heart, that he not forget from his heart the matter of the Sabbath, because of its allusion to the world that is entirely long [the World to Come] as compared to the world that is entirely Sabbath - and even when only one portion happens to come to him, by designating it for the Sabbath he eats it for the sake of the Sabbath, for since it was possible for him to eat it and not leave it for the honor of the Sabbath, it follows that he eats it for the sake of the holiness of the Sabbath; and likewise, when he designates the second one for the Sabbath and does not eat it, it follows that he eats the first one for the honor of the Sabbath, since he left the second one. And it follows from this that the end of the deed reflects the beginning of the thought - for in the supernal thought, the Sabbath preceded, and afterward the six days of labor, but at the end of the deed, then the beginning of the thought is revealed - and therefore, every single day, the Sabbath comes first in his thought, and he sets his heart to eat in honor of the Sabbath, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:107: Also, when a person gives from his meal to a poor person, his meal is a mitzvah - and so Rabbi Tanchum used to do, as explained in the Midrash, Vayikra Rabbah (Parashat Behar 34:5), on the verse "and if your brother becomes poor" (Leviticus 25:35) - these are its words: this is what Rabbi Tanchum son of Rabbi Chiya used to do: when his mother would buy him one litra of meat from the market, she would buy for herself two - one for the poor and one for him - because of (Ecclesiastes 7:14), "God has made the one as well as the other," the poor and the rich, so that they might benefit from one another - therefore Moses warns Israel, "and if your brother becomes poor" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:108: Now, through this a person shall be saved so that his belly not turn over upon his face in his grave after three days, as they said in the Zohar (Parashat Vayakhel, page 199b) - these are its words: after three days, that filth turns over upon its face and says to him, take back what you gave me - you ate and drank every day and did not give to the poor, and all your days were like festivals and holidays, while the poor were hungry and did not eat with you - take back what you gave me. This is what is written (Malachi 2:3), "and I will spread dung upon your faces, the dung of your festivals" - and this has already been established - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:109: And in the Zohar (Parashat Vayakhel, page 218a) it is explained that during the six weekdays the Shechinah enjoys the Grace After Meals, but on the Sabbath the Shechinah enjoys the very meal itself that a person delights in, for everything a person delights in on the Sabbath he performs a mitzvah - and along these lines also, "the soul of the righteous eats to satisfy his soul," meaning that his soul, which is the Shechinah, is satisfied from the Grace After Meals. These are its words: Rabbi Yosei opened and said (Ruth 3:7), "and Boaz ate and drank and his heart was merry" - what is "his heart was merry"? That he blessed over his food, as they established - and this is the secret that whoever blesses over his food thereby gladdens his heart - and who is this? As it is written (Psalms 27:8), "to You my heart says," and it is written (ibid. 73:26), "the rock of my heart and my portion" - for the blessing over food is beloved before the Holy One, blessed be He; whoever blesses over satiety gladdens and rejoices another place, and your sign is: the meal of the Sabbath, in another place, enjoys from that blessing of satiety. Why? Because sustenance is difficult before the Holy One, blessed be He, in that place, and once a person eats and drinks and blesses that blessing, it ascends and enjoys those words of satiety, and it is found that it enjoys from sustenance below and from above - and this is the secret known to the colleagues: the secret is, on a weekday it enjoys only from those words that ascend from satiety, and all of them are crowned and filled and satisfied with joy, and that place enjoys from them. On the Sabbath it is another secret, in the actual food itself, and in that joy of the food of the mitzvah of Sabbath they established this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:110: Whoever blesses the Holy One, blessed be He, from satiety must direct his heart and set his desire in joy, and should not be found sad, but rather bless in joy through this secret, and set his desire, for he now gives to another in joy and with a good eye - just as he blesses in joy and with a good eye, so shall he be given in joy and with a good eye - and therefore he should not be found sad at all, but rather in joy and with words of Torah, and set his heart and his desire to give this blessing with the secret that is needed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:111: The secret here: the four chariots ruling in the four directions are nourished from that blessing of satiety, and through those words "Blessed are You," they enjoy and grow and are crowned by it - and whoever blesses needs his desire in joy and with a good eye, and concerning this, "he who has a good eye shall be blessed" (Proverbs 22:9) - and here it descends to the end of the verse, "for he gives of his bread to the poor" - for if you do not say so, the beginning of this verse would not match its end nor its end its beginning; rather, "he who has a good eye" as established, "shall be blessed" certainly with a good eye and in joy, and it is not for nothing that he blesses in joy, for from that blessing and from that joy "he gives of his bread to the poor" - a place to be nourished from all directions, a place that has nothing of its own, a place that enjoys from all directions and is included from all directions - these matters are entrusted only to the wise, to know the way of Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:112: Come and see, Boaz had a good eye, and there was no harshness of brow in him toward the world at all - what is written? (Ruth 3:7) "and he went to lie down at the end of the heap of grain" - the secret is as it is written (Song of Songs 7:3), "your belly is a heap of wheat" - from here we learn that whoever blesses the Grace After Meals properly, in joy, with the desire of the heart, when he ascends from this world, a place is prepared for him among supernal secrets in holy chambers - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:113: And when you understand what it said, "and it is found that it enjoys from sustenance and from above," which is through what is explained in Parashat Noach (page 60a-b) on the verse (Proverbs 5:15), "drink water from your own cistern" - you shall understand the sweetness of the honeycomb's nectar, "the righteous eats to satisfy his soul." And we intended to copy the whole teaching, because in it is explained the intent of the Grace After Meals in what it said, "the secret here: the four chariots ruling in the four directions are nourished from that blessing of satiety," and so on - and therefore his reward in the World to Come, in what it said at the end of the teaching, "a place is prepared for him among supernal secrets in holy chambers." Also what it said, that he should bless "with a good eye" - its meaning is understood from what it said in the Idra (Parashat Naso, page 130a), that "good of eye" refers to Arich [Anpin], see there - and for this he needs a good eye and desire and joy, in order to bestow flow from the first three [sefirot].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 15:114: Now, if a person intends, at the start of eating, that he eats in order to bless the place that needs the blessing, so that flow be bestowed from above - this is like the parable of the nursing mother: when she has someone to nurse, the milk increases in her breasts - this too is a correct intent, and it is along the lines of what is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Beshalach, page 62a), that a person is obligated to ask for his sustenance every day, for since he asks, he causes sustenance to be bestowed from above in order that it be bestowed to him - and it is already known that sustenance depends on mazal [supernal fortune], as it is said (Mo'ed Katan 28a), "children, life, and sustenance... but depend on mazal," and so on. It said, these are its words: Rabbi Yosei opened, (Psalms 145:16), "You open Your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing" - what is written above it? "the eyes of all look to You" - all those beings of the world watch and lift their eyes to the Holy One, blessed be He - therefore all these people of faith need, every single day, to ask for their sustenance from the Holy One, blessed be He, and to pray their prayer before Him. Why? Because whoever prays his prayer to the Holy One, blessed be He, for his sustenance causes that tree, from which sustenance goes forth to all, to be blessed every day - and the reason for the matter is "blessed is the LORD, day by day" (Psalms 68:20) - even though he is found with Him [already sustained], he must ask before the Holy One, blessed be He, and pray for sustenance every day, so that blessings be found with Him every single day above. And therefore a person should not cook food from one day for another day, and should not delay from one day to another - this is what is written (Exodus 16:4), "and the people went out and gathered a portion for each day," except for the eve of the Sabbath for the Sabbath, as has been established - and then the Holy One, blessed be He, is found full of blessings every day, and then it is written, "You open Your hand," and so on. What is "desire" [ratzon]? That desire found from the Holy Ancient One, from which desire goes forth for sustenance to be found for all - and whoever asks for sustenance every single day is called a faithful child, a child for whose sake blessings are found above - to this point.
